topic: Engineering the harness around AI agents: context management, tool protocols (including MCP), sandboxing and permissions, memory, evaluation and benchmarks, multi-agent orchestration, and observability
audience: Engineers and technical leads building agent products or agent infrastructure (coding agents, computer-use agents, agent SDKs and frameworks, MCP servers). They already understand tool calling, context windows, evals, and sandboxing basics; they want evidence-based reading on what changed and what to do about it.
central_question: What changed this month in how AI agent harnesses are built, evaluated, and operated, and which of those changes should practitioners act on?
voice: Skeptical, evidence-first, practitioner-to-practitioner. Separates announcements from measured results, labels interpretation as interpretation, names uncertainty plainly, and never manufactures disagreement.

series.01: What changed, and which developments matter most to this audience?
series.02: Which claims withstand scrutiny, and where are the evidence or interpretations in tension?
series.03: What do these developments imply for the audience, and what should they watch next?

includes: harness design: agent loops, context management, compaction, memory, planning and sub-agent orchestration
tool interfaces and protocols: MCP, tool search, function calling conventions, computer use
safety rails in the harness: sandboxing, permissions, approvals, guardrails, prompt-injection defenses
evaluation of agents: benchmarks, eval harnesses, trajectory analysis, cost and latency measurement
operating agents in production: observability, tracing, reliability, cost control, deployment patterns
research results that change how harnesses should be built
excludes: model releases or benchmark scores with no harness or integration implication
consumer product news, funding and hiring news, conference marketing
generic prompt-engineering tips, beginner tutorials, listicles
policy and regulation unless it changes what a harness must enforce

return_reason: Each edition is a dated, evidence-linked digest: readers can see exactly which sources changed the picture since the last edition, which vendor claims held up, and what to watch next.
